note: Plain-Solid misuse patterns from application code, each with a correct twin. Run through benchmarks/reviewed-package-models/development/misuse-runtime-ledger.mjs --cases; built by build_cases.py.

cases.why: A signal read in the component body sees its value once.
A memo read in the component body sees its value once.
A store property read in the component body sees its value once.
Seeding a signal from another in the body reads it untracked (the donegeon shape).
An `if` on a signal in the body is evaluated once.
A helper called from the body reads the signal in the body's extent.
A local hook that reads its argument in the call reads it in the body.
Mapping a store array in the body reads every element once.
Spreading a store into a plain object reads every property once.
A child reading its prop in its body sees the parent's signal once.
Destructuring props in the parameter reads them once.
A read in an effect's apply callback is untracked.
A store read in an effect's apply callback is untracked.
A read in a For child's render function body is evaluated once per row.
A read in a keyed Show child's function body is evaluated once.
A render-prop callback the child calls in its body reads the signal during render.
A read in an onSettled callback is untracked.
A signal written inside a memo's compute.
A signal written directly in the component body.
A signal written inside a tracked JSX expression.
A signal written inside an effect's compute function.
onCleanup after an await runs with no owner.
An effect created from a timer has no owner.
onCleanup from a timer has no owner.
An effect created in a promise continuation has no owner.
onCleanup inside createTrackedEffect, a leaf owner.
A primitive created inside createTrackedEffect, a leaf owner.
A memo created inside onSettled, a leaf owner.
A helper called from an effect's apply callback reads a signal in that untracked extent.
A hook called in the body reads a signal it created, in its own body.
A hook called in the body reads the accessor it receives, in its own body.
